desc:
There are numCourses courses numbered 0 to numCourses - 1. Each entry prerequisites[i] = [a, b] means course b must be completed before course a can be taken. Pairs may repeat. You take one course at a time.

Return an order in which all courses can be taken so that every course comes after all of its prerequisites. Often many orders work, so return the lexicographically smallest one: comparing two orders, look at the first position where they differ, and the order with the smaller course number there is smaller.

If the courses cannot all be completed because of a circular dependency, return an empty array.

numCourses = 4, prerequisites = [[1,0],[2,0],[3,1],[3,2]] -> [0,1,2,3]
numCourses = 3, prerequisites = [[0,1],[1,2]]             -> [2,1,0]
numCourses = 3, prerequisites = [[1,0],[2,0]]             -> [0,1,2]
numCourses = 2, prerequisites = [[0,1],[1,0]]             -> []
constraints: 0 ≤ a, b < numCourses; a pair may name the same course twice (that makes the answer empty)
hints: Which courses can you take first? Once you take one, which other courses may become available?
Count, for every course, how many of its prerequisites are still missing. A course is available when that count is 0. Taking a course lowers the count of every course that depends on it.

Several courses can be available at once. Always pick the smallest available number: keep the available courses in a min-heap. If you finish with fewer than numCourses courses taken, a cycle blocks the rest, so return an empty array.
editorial: This is Kahn's topological sort. Build for every course the list of courses that depend on it, and the number of unmet prerequisites (indeg). Start with all courses of indegree 0, take one, and decrease the indegree of its dependents; any dependent reaching 0 becomes available.

To get the lexicographically smallest order, make the choice at each step greedily: take the smallest available number. This is correct because any course that is available now will still be available later (availability never disappears), so placing the smallest one first can only be compared with orders that place a larger one first, and swapping the smaller course forward keeps the order valid and makes it smaller. A min-heap supplies the smallest available course in O(log n).

If the loop ends with fewer than numCourses courses taken, the remaining courses all have an unmet prerequisite inside the remaining set, which means they lie on or behind a cycle; return []. Repeated pairs are counted twice in the indegree and decreased twice, so they cause no trouble. Time is O((n + m) log n), space O(n + m).
solution:
import heapq


def findOrder(numCourses, prerequisites):
    adj = [[] for _ in range(numCourses)]
    indeg = [0] * numCourses
    for a, b in prerequisites:
        adj[b].append(a)
        indeg[a] += 1
    heap = [i for i in range(numCourses) if indeg[i] == 0]
    heapq.heapify(heap)
    order = []
    while heap:
        u = heapq.heappop(heap)
        order.append(u)
        for v in adj[u]:
            indeg[v] -= 1
            if indeg[v] == 0:
                heapq.heappush(heap, v)
    return order if len(order) == numCourses else []
